GLOSSARY

Alcohol Use Disorder Identification Test (AUDIT): a 10-item tool developed by the World Health
Organization. Patients should use a standard drink volume/strength to answer questions, with a score of 8
or more considered harmful alcohol use.

Alcohol use disorders: disorders related to drinking alcohol-containing beverages.

CAGE: commonly used 4-question screening tool to help determine if problematic substance use exists. It is an
acronym of Cutting down, Annoyance to Criticism, Guilty feeling, and Eye openers. The CAGE questions focus
on alcohol and the CAGE-AID (CAGE questions adapted to include drug use) focuses on other substances in
addition to alcohol. While popular and easy to implement, this tool focuses on alcohol dependence more than
problematic alcohol use, and other tools, such as AUDIT, are now more commonly recommended.

CRAFFT: screening tool designed to help identify issues around substances for those between the age of
12 and 21. The name of the tool is a mnemonic of several of the test questions: Car, Relax, Alone, Forget,
Friends, Trouble.

Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition, Text Revision (DSM-5-TR):
published by the American Psychiatric Association, this manual codifies classifications and diagnostic
criteria used by mental health professionals in the US.

E-cigarette or vaping associated lung injury (EVALI): lung disease associated with the use of vaping
products that can be severe and life-threatening. Symptoms can initially mimic common pulmonary
diagnoses like pneumonia, but individuals typically do not respond to antibiotic therapy. Individuals usually
seek care within a few days to several weeks when symptoms first arise. EVALI remains a diagnosis of
exclusion because, at present, no specific test or marker exists for its diagnosis, and evaluation should be
guided by clinical judgment.

Heaviness of Smoking Index (HSI): a test index used to measure how heavily an individual smokes and
to assess degree of nicotine addiction. HSI was derived from the Fagerstrém Test for Nicotine Dependence.

Modified Single Alcohol Screening Questionnaire (MSASQ): an alcohol harm assessment tool that
takes a single question from the AUDIT tool and uses a scoring system of 0-4 (0 = never, 4 = daily or
almost daily), where a score of 2 or above is positive. If positive, the AUDIT tool allows a full scoring.

National Institute for Drug Abuse (NIDA): institute within the US Department of Health and Human
Services whose goal is to advance addiction science.

Nicotine: a highly addictive chemical used in tobacco products. Nicotine dependence is the most common
form of chemical dependence in the US.

Nicotine replacement therapy (NRT): medications that are used to help people quit smoking by
providing nicotine to the user.

NIDA-Modified Alcohol, Smoking, and Substance Involvement Screening Test (NMASSIST): a
test appropriate for adult patients that can be completed in clinic during an interview or by the patient on
their own. Also known as the NIDA Quick Screen.
